name: app-header
source: layout/header.vue (the global top bar), split from the product Toolbars family
summary: The GLOBAL top bar present on every authenticated page, and the COMPOSITION HOST for the App Chrome family: the brand/logo on the left, and on the right the interactive surfaces — global search, notifications, and the user account menu — plus a BUILD version tag. Two ways to fill the right side: (1) the INTERACTIVE composition (drop obs-command-palette, obs-notification-menu, obs-user-menu into the slots — each opens its own surface on click; this is how the product's bar works), or (2) the PRESENTATIONAL `actions` prop (declarative circular icon-buttons that fire an `action` event but open nothing — for a simple static header). App CHROME — a SEPARATE archetype from obs-page-header (the per-page title bar); pairs with obs-sidebar (the left module nav). Bar: 50px tall, --page-background-color, a --border-color bottom rule. Circular buttons 36×36 (--neutral-light; --primary when active); notification badge --secondary-red; avatar --primary.

variants.name: interactive-chrome
variants.what: the whole App Chrome family composed in the slots — obs-command-palette (overlay/Cmd+K) + obs-notification-menu + obs-user-menu — each opening its own surface on click
variants.usage: the real product top bar; the default recommendation

variants.name: presentational-actions
variants.what: static circular icon-buttons via the `actions` prop (JSON) — fire an `action` event, open no panel
variants.usage: a simple non-interactive header, or when you wire the surfaces yourself

variants.name: default
variants.what: brand + action icons + build tag + user avatar

variants.name: with-badge
variants.what: a count badge on an action (e.g. notifications)

variants.name: logo
variants.what: a logo in the brand slot instead of text

variants.name: wordmark
variants.what: a text brand via the `brand` prop when there is no logo image

sizes.name: default
sizes.note: the global bar is a fixed 50px tall (matches the product @navbar-height); circular action buttons 36×36, the user avatar 32×32, the BUILD tag 22px. No size variants — one global chrome height.

brand.note: brand text on the left (18px / weight 700 / --primary-alt / letter-spacing .5px). For a logo image use the `brand` slot instead.

actions.note: the right-side action buttons — a JSON array of {icon,label,badge?,active?}. Each renders a 36×36 circular icon button (reuses obs-icon); `badge` shows a --secondary-red count; `active` highlights it --primary. Clicking one fires `action`.

build.note: the BUILD version tag text, e.g. "8.0.0" → renders "BUILD : 8.0.0" (--timerange-background-color / --primary).

user.note: user initials for the avatar (32×32, --primary). For the account dropdown use the `user` slot (drop an obs-menu).

events.action: ({icon,label,index}) — a right-side action icon-button was clicked.
events.user: () — the fallback avatar (user attribute) was clicked/activated. Handle it to open your account menu, or use the `user` slot with obs-user-menu for a turnkey menu.

slots.brand: a custom brand logo (/obs-logo). If omitted AND the `brand` text prop is empty, the DEFAULT FULL ObserveOps logo (obs-logo name="motadata_full" — mark + wordmark) renders.
slots.default: extra custom actions inserted between the icon buttons and the build tag / user.
slots.user: a custom user control — drop an obs-menu for the account/logout dropdown, replacing the initials avatar.

decisionFlow: The GLOBAL bar at the very top of every page (logo + global search + notifications + user)? -> obs-app-header.
The per-PAGE title bar (title + count + page actions)? -> obs-page-header, NOT app-header.
The left module/primary navigation? -> obs-sidebar (app-header is the horizontal counterpart).
A left-nav trail / in-page section switch? -> obs-breadcrumbs / obs-tabs.
Want the header to actually WORK (each icon opens a panel)? -> use the INTERACTIVE composition: drop the App Chrome elements into the slots (below), not the `actions` prop.
The global SEARCH / command omnibox (Cmd+K)? -> put an obs-command-palette (overlay) in the default slot — the 🔍 opens a centered modal.
The notifications bell + dropdown panel? -> put an obs-notification-menu in the default slot (it renders its own bell + badge + panel).
The account dropdown from the avatar? -> put an obs-user-menu (turnkey: profile/setup/docs + theme switch + logout) in the `user` slot; for a bespoke list use an obs-menu instead.
Just a simple, non-interactive header (no panels)? -> the `actions` prop (presentational circular icons) + the `user` initials avatar.

interactive-chrome.useWhen: the real product top bar — you want clicking search / bell / avatar to actually open their surfaces. Compose the three App Chrome elements in the slots.
interactive-chrome.dontUse: when you only need static icons that fire an event you handle yourself (use `actions`).
interactive-chrome.example: <obs-app-header><obs-command-palette overlay …></obs-command-palette><obs-notification-menu count="3" …></obs-notification-menu><obs-user-menu slot="user" …></obs-user-menu></obs-app-header> — 🔍 opens the Cmd+K modal, 🔔 the alerts panel, avatar the account menu.

presentational-actions.useWhen: a simple non-interactive header, or when the surfaces are wired elsewhere and you only need the icon row + an `action` event.
presentational-actions.dontUse: when you want the panels to open on click — compose the interactive elements instead.

default.useWhen: the global chrome of an authenticated app shell — one per app, on every page.
default.dontUse: as a page-level header (title + page actions) -> obs-page-header.
default.example: brand "motadata" + search/health/approval/notifications + BUILD tag + user avatar.

with-badge.useWhen: an action carries a live count (unread notifications / approvals).
with-badge.dontUse: a plain action with no count.

active-route.useWhen: highlight the action for the current route/section.
active-route.dontUse: when no action maps to the current page.
active-route.example: the Health action is active on the health page ({active:true} → --primary).

logo.useWhen: a real product/tenant logo image belongs in the bar.
logo.dontUse: when a wordmark/text brand is enough (use the brand prop).

wordmark.useWhen: there is no logo image — render the product/tenant name as text (18px / weight 700 / --primary-alt).
wordmark.dontUse: when a logo image exists (use the `brand` slot); the slot wins over the prop.

brand.useWhen: leave brand unset to get the DEFAULT ObserveOps logo; set the `brand` slot for a custom logo, or the `brand` text prop for a wordmark.
brand.dontUse: expecting an empty brand area when nothing is passed — it now falls back to the ObserveOps mark (like obs-sidebar).
brand.example: → shows the ObserveOps logo; → text; → custom logo

a11y.summary: The bar renders as a <header> landmark. Presentational actions are real <button>s with an aria-label/title (the icon is decorative); the count badge sits inside the button (announced with its label). In the INTERACTIVE composition each slotted element owns its own a11y contract — obs-command-palette manages the Cmd+K modal focus/Esc, obs-notification-menu and obs-user-menu render their own keyboard-navigable popovers with roles — so prefer those over the bare `user` initials avatar (which is only a role=button). One app-header per app; don't nest landmarks.

issues.issue: The count badge is a small overlay on the bell — ensure the surrounding button's aria-label conveys the count (e.g. "Notifications, 3 unread") for screen readers, since the visual "3" alone is easy to miss.

knownIssues.issue: The action set is data-driven (the `actions` prop) rather than the fixed product list, so it is reusable; the real header also has route-aware active states and a global command-search overlay wired to the app router — those bindings are the consumer's (obs-app-header renders the chrome + fires `action`).

usedIn: The top of every authenticated app layout — the global chrome above all page content (layout/header.vue).

Left: the product/tenant brand (Motadata logo, or a text wordmark). Right: global search · health monitoring · approval · the notifications bell (with an unread count) · a BUILD version tag · the user account menu.
The current-route action highlights --primary (e.g. the Health icon on the health dashboard).
Pairs with obs-sidebar (the vertical module nav) to form the app shell; per-page titles/actions live in obs-page-header, not here.
do: Use as the GLOBAL top bar / app chrome on every authenticated page — brand (left) + global actions + user (right).
Give an action a `badge` for a live count (notifications / approvals); mark the current-route action `active` (→ --primary).
Put an obs-menu in the `user` slot for the account dropdown; a logo in the `brand` slot (theme-toggled).
Drive the action buttons from the `actions` prop (reuses obs-icon) and handle clicks via the `action` event.
dont: Don’t use as a per-page header (title + page actions) — that is obs-page-header.
Don’t use for the left module/primary navigation — that is obs-sidebar (app-header is the horizontal counterpart).
Don’t hand-build the circular icon buttons / avatar — the component renders the chrome; wire routing/search to your app.
Don’t place more than one per app — it is the single global chrome.
